questions.q: Why does the chapter say testing an impression is faith, not doubt?
options: Because God never speaks today
Because Scripture commands examination precisely because God speaks and we are fallible receivers (1 Thessalonians 5:20–21; Acts 17:11)
Because retreats are unreliable
Because only pastors can hear God
questions.explanation: Paul holds both together: do not despise prophecies, and test everything. Testing honours God by refusing to attach his name to what may be our own fear, desire or exhaustion.

options: Testing can be skipped if you feel certain
Waiting and consulting do not apply to immediate danger, abuse, urgent medical care, legal reporting duties, or deadlines that cannot safely be postponed
Safety concerns should be tested for a month first
Only pastors decide what is safe
questions.explanation: Do not remain in danger merely to complete a discernment process. Chapter 5's guidance on abuse and crisis takes precedence.

questions.q: Into which three categories are the cards sorted?
options: Past, present, future
Nothing significant; a low-risk reversible step; a major, high-impact or hard-to-reverse direction
Spiritual, practical, relational
Confirmed, doubtful, rejected
questions.explanation: Most of what people bring home is in the second category. Category three gets the full testing, over weeks, with other people, before any action.

questions.q: Which test is described as the first and weightiest?
options: Whether it feels peaceful
Whether your Eli agrees
Whether it agrees with Scripture read in context, not merely a matching verse
Whether a sign confirms it
questions.explanation: Ask what the whole of Scripture teaches about the kind of thing you are considering. An impression that contradicts clear biblical teaching fails here and nothing else needs checking.

questions.q: Which of these is a warning sign rather than a confirmation, according to test seven?
options: "I would like wise people to examine this"
"They would not understand; this is between me and God"
"Let me take a smaller reversible step first"
"I will give this a month"
questions.explanation: Secrecy, superiority, urgency that exists mainly to prevent examination, and immunity from challenge are warning signs. Genuine direction from God can bear examination.

questions.q: What does the chapter say about Gideon's fleece (Judges 6:36–40)?
options: It is the recommended way to confirm guidance
It is recorded, not commended; Gideon already had God's clear word and was asking for reassurance
It proves God always gives signs
It should be repeated three times
questions.explanation: Signs are easy to manufacture and misread. Seek confirmation through Scripture, truthful examination, wise counsel, time, prayer and fruit.

reflection: Which category does your card fall into? If nothing significant, go to Chapter 14 with a clear conscience.
Does the safety exception apply to anything? If so, what help are you seeking today?
When will you contact your Eli, and what will you bring?
What is the smallest reversible version of any step you are considering?
Is there anything you are reluctant to test? Write down why. Reluctance to test is itself something to test.
